messages:
Nina: Quick heads-up — bringup of ranky-3b int8 (adaptive quant config v2) on the short+long holdout shows NDCG down ~3.4 pts vs fp16 across the mixed cohort. Not seeing a big MRR change, mostly NDCG drop concentrated in long-doc queries (>1k tokens).

Matt: ugh. do you have the exact slice numbers and seed? is this on the same candidate pool?

Nina: slice = holdout-mix-2026-03, 12k queries; long-doc bucket = 1.2k queries. seed=42 for the original run. candidate pool identical afaict (we use the cached candidates from the ingestion job).

Priya: can you paste the eval command and quant config? wondering if per-layer vs per-tensor rounding changed distribution.

Nina: sure — running command:
```
./eval_rerank.py --model ranky-3b --weights quant/v2/hybrid.ckpt --holdout holdout-mix-2026-03 --batch 64 --seed 42 --report ndcg,mrr --slice longdoc
```
quant config snippet:
```json
{"quant_type": "adaptive", "bits": 8, "per_channel": true, "kv_pack": "auto", "fallback_fp16_thresh": 0.02}
```

Sam: curious: kv_pack = auto could choose a different layout vs fp16 runtime. Also hybrid per-layer rounding sometimes blows up attention score stability for long contexts. did the int8 runtime change the KV cache packing order?

Nina: good call. we recently landed a small optimization that reorders kv storage to improve memory locality. It only flips on for "auto" when sequence avg > 512.

EvalBot: automated-run-summary: run=6180009999, model=ranky-3b-int8-adaptive-v2, ndcg_all=0.624, ndcg_long=0.532, mrr_all=0.421, seed=42, duration=2h14m

Priya: compare to the fp16 baseline?

Nina: baseline fp16 (same seed) -> ndcg_all=0.658, ndcg_long=0.566, mrr_all=0.426

Matt: so delta ndcg_long = -0.034 absolute (~6% relative). that's notable. can we reproduce by forcing kv_pack=false and disabling the kv reorder?

Sam: also try per_channel=false (per-tensor) — sometimes per_channel with hybrid rounding creates bigger biases on attention logits for longer sequences.

Priya: agree. also rule out holdout leakage: can we re-run a quick oracle check to ensure the holdout candidate pool wasn't accidentally deduped/reshuffled between baseline and quant runs? command to diff doc ids:
```
python -c "from harness import load_candidates; a=load_candidates('holdout-mix-2026-03','fp16'); b=load_candidates('holdout-mix-2026-03','int8'); print(len(set(a.ids)-set(b.ids)))"
```

Nina: ran that — zero diffs. candidate pools identical.

Matt: ok. Nina, can you kick two quick re-runs: 1) int8 with kv_pack=false + kv_reorder disabled; 2) int8 with per_channel=false. keep seed same, smaller batch if needed. throw logs here.

Nina: starting both now. approximate ETA 45m. tagging @Sam and @Priya for quick eyes.

Sam: will watch for top-k flips. sometimes NDCG drop is from rank swaps in tail that don't affect top1 much.

EvalBot: run-started: 6180010001 variant=kv_off

EvalBot: run-started: 6180010005 variant=per_tensor

Nina: quick interim: kv_off run finished early — ndcg_all=0.646, ndcg_long=0.559, mrr_all=0.424. That's much closer to fp16.

Priya: promising — kv_pack appears to be the main culprit. can you capture the top-10 diffs for the long-doc bucket?

Nina: pasted a small diff snippet:
```
query_id: Q12345
fp16_top3: [D17, D9, D101]
int8_auto_top3: [D9, D17, D101]
score_fp16: [0.87,0.85,0.80]
score_int8: [0.88,0.84,0.79]
```
Notes: flips between D17 and D9 at positions 1/2 for several queries.

Matt: those look like small score perturbations causing rank swaps. but NDCG delta still measurable across many queries. can we test a deterministic micro-benchmark: run a subset (200 queries) with binary diffs of attention logits on fp16 vs int8+kvpack to see where largest per-token divergence occurs.

Sam: I'll prep a script to dump attention logit histograms and L2 diffs for the top layers. if kv packing reorder changes layout, we might be reading different aligned memory resulting in subtle permutation of float->int conversion order.

Priya: if kv_pack auto is intended to be default, we should update our onboarding checklist: require the quant config to be explicitly set for holdout runs, and include kv_pack parity check between baseline and quant.

Nina: agreed — opened a quick PR to docs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-evals/pull/482

Matt: nice. follow-ups: Sam, can you run the micro-benchmark? Priya, can you add the kv parity CI gate for onboarding? I'll add a note to the bringup playbook about checking long-doc slices specifically for quant changes.

Sam: running micro-bench now, will post results.

EvalBot: run-finished: 6180010025 variant=per_tensor ndcg_all=0.651 ndcg_long=0.561 mrr_all=0.425 duration=46m

Nina: per_tensor also improved vs auto: ndcg_long=0.561 (but kv_off was slightly better). conclusion: adaptive-auto + kv_pack interaction caused ordering/packing that amplified small quantization noise on long contexts.

Priya: thanks — action items: 1) default onboarding to kv_pack=false for initial int8 comparisons (low-risk), 2) add kv packing parity test to QA harness, 3) document sequence-length triggered config flips in the runtime so quantization owners are aware. I'll raise a JIRA.

Matt: great work triaging quickly. this is a helpful reminder that runtime heuristics (auto toggles) must be explicitly controlled during evals. :thumbsup:

Nina: thanks everyone. will update the bringup ticket with full logs and PR link.

Sam: posted micro-bench gist with layer-wise L2 diffs: https://gist.github.com/sam/kvpack-int8-layer-diffs (short summary: largest diffs in layers 10-12 around kv index offsets)

Priya: perfect. I'll draft the CI change and loop in infra to add a kv parity check into the pre-onboard smoke.

Nina: closing the loop here — re-run for official report tomorrow with locked kv_pack=false and per_tensor as ablation. thanks all.
